crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: AI and Authorship
children.blurb: AI and authorship concerns the question of who counts as an author when generative models or other AI systems contribute to research, writing, or data analysis.

children.name: Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking
children.blurb: Fabricated citations and fact checking concerns the detection and prevention of references that do not exist, misattribute sources, or misrepresent what a source says.

children.name: Training Data and Academic Work
children.blurb: Training data and academic work covers the use of scholarly texts, including journal articles, preprints, theses, and course materials, as inputs for machine learning systems.

children.name: Ethics Review with AI Assistance
children.blurb: Ethics review with AI assistance covers the use of machine learning and natural language tools to support institutional review boards, research ethics committees, and journal editors in screening protocols, identifying risks, checking consent language, and flagging conflicts or missing safeguards.

children.name: Provenance of Research Images and Data
children.blurb: Provenance of research images and data is the record of where a dataset or image came from, how it was created or collected, who modified it, and under what conditions it can be reused.

sections.body: This field covers how AI systems are used and misused in the production and checking of scholarly work. Right now, large language models draft sections of papers, suggest author lists, and generate summaries, while separate tools attempt to detect AI-written text and verify citations. Researchers are using automated fact checking against databases of published claims, and some groups are building provenance logs for training data and research images. The work is practical: it deals with real authorship disputes, fake references that look real, and images that have been altered or reused without credit. It also includes ethics review, where AI helps screen proposals for obvious risks or missing consent statements. The focus is on what can be checked, logged, and traced in a research record.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of this work is uneven. Detecting AI generated text is not solved; current tools produce both false positives and false negatives, and a determined author can often rewrite past them. Fabricated citations are a known problem, and fact checking tools catch some but not all, especially when a fake reference points to a real journal with a plausible title. Training data provenance is improving for large public datasets, but many academic models still lack a complete record of where their data came from. Ethics review with AI assistance is mostly at the screening stage, not the decision stage, because reviewers still need to judge context and harm. Provenance of research images and data is stronger for fields that already use persistent identifiers, but weaker for older or informally shared material, and no current system can guarantee a paper is clean, only that certain checks have been run.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages under this section move from who gets credit to how evidence is verified. AI and Authorship looks at what counts as a human contribution when a model drafts or revises text, while Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking covers the specific failure of invented references and the tools that compare citations against databases of published work. Training Data and Academic Work explains how the material used to train models affects what they produce, and why a missing data record matters for reproducibility. Ethics Review with AI Assistance describes where automated screening helps and where human judgment remains necessary, and Provenance of Research Images and Data closes the loop by showing how to track an image or dataset from creation to publication. A reader would start with authorship to understand responsibility, then move through citation checking and training data to see how errors enter the record, and finish with ethics review and provenance to see how institutions try to catch those errors before and after publication. The site's library of 135 research papers and 11,222 extracted claims sits behind these pages, so each page links to the original work rather than a secondary search tool.
